sources.title: Albert Schwarz and Oleg Zaboronsky, Supersymmetry and localization
sources.locator: Complete 16-page paper retrieved. Section 2, PDF pp. 2–3, on ΠTM, odd vector fields, and the invariant Berezin volume; Section 3, PDF pp. 4–7, Theorem 1 statement and complete proof, including div(dV)Q=0, compactness, Q-squared conditions, and vanishing integrals of Q-exact terms.

contents.name: Odd tangent bundle and finite-dimensional Q data
contents.support: The source identifies odd tangent-bundle functions with forms and describes odd-vector-field integration data. The local definition states the actual field bundles, domains, Q-square, regulator, symbol, and zero-mode conventions used here.

contents.name: Compact finite-dimensional localization theorem and its extra hypotheses
contents.support: The source proves a distinct fixed-locus theorem under compact-supermanifold and Q-volume hypotheses. This batch uses it only to delimit finite-dimensional scope; the conditional deformation-invariance proof is supplied by the exact local finite theorem, not imported from this paper.

sources.title: Vasily Pestun and Maxim Zabzine, Introduction to localization in quantum field theory
sources.locator: Complete 19-page chapter retrieved. Section 1, PDF pp. 1–3: ΠTM formulation, the Q-exact finite-dimensional deformation, Stokes-based t-independence for δ²W=0, the subsequent saddle limit, and the caveat that infinite-dimensional extensions require all formal steps to be defined.

contents.name: Finite-dimensional Q-exact deformation and separation from the saddle limit
contents.support: The review treats Q-exact parameter independence on finite-dimensional ΠTM data and separates it from the additional t-to-infinity saddle calculation. It states that infinite-dimensional extensions require the formal steps and determinants to be defined.

contents.name: Odd tangent-bundle and integration setup
contents.support: The review describes finite-dimensional odd tangent-bundle integration and flags the distinct differential-operator and determinant issues in the infinite-dimensional case.

sources.title: Gerald B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Complete book text retrieved. Chapter 2, §2.27, printed pp. 55–56: parts (a)–(b), with the full sequential dominated-convergence proof for differentiation under the integral sign and the note that the estimate may be taken on a compact subinterval of an open parameter interval.

contents.name: Differentiation under the integral sign with a uniform L1 majorant
contents.support: The textbook theorem differentiates the integral when sections are integrable and the parameter derivative has one L1 majorant on the interval. The physical theorem adopts the exact hypotheses of the inspected finite-dimensional supplier, which localizes this estimate on compact parameter subintervals.

sources.title: Vasily Pestun, Localization of Gauge Theory on a Four-Sphere and Supersymmetric Wilson Loops
sources.locator: §1 equations (1.3)–(1.4) and S4 noncommutative-regulator caveat; §2 equations (2.1)–(2.14), (2.26)–(2.30); §4.1–§4.3 equations (4.1)–(4.15); Appendix C equations (C.1)–(C.17).
sources.actual_read_extent: Retrieved the full 58-page PDF. Read the S4 action, ten-dimensional reduction and Euclidean contour; the conformal Killing-spinor solution and selected N=2 subalgebra; the seven-auxiliary one-generator off-shell transformations and Appendix C closure calculation; the Faddeev–Popov zero-mode treatment, gauge-fixing slice, combined supersymmetry/BRST complex and Q-square; and the introduction's explicit statement that the noncommutative S4 deformation is assumed rather than constructed.
sources.limitations: The paper's continuum path integral and determinant/localization formula are not independently reconstructed here. The S4 regulator extension remains the author's stated assumption. Its off-shell completion closes the selected localizing generator, not every hypermultiplet supersymmetry off shell.

contents.name: S4 model conventions, gauge fixing, and total Q-square
contents.locator: Section 2, equations (2.5)–(2.14), (2.26)–(2.30); Sections 4.2–4.3, equations (4.4)–(4.15); Section 1, printed/PDF p.4, unnumbered regulator paragraph between (1.5) and (1.6).
contents.support: The paper supplies source conventions for the round-sphere off-shell transformation, gauge fixing, and symmetry square. The local definition distinguishes the field-space fluctuation data and does not infer ellipticity or a determinant.

contents.name: Q-exact deformation and boundary term
contents.support: The paper states that a Q-squared-invariant V gives Q-exact deformation independence up to a boundary contribution and then separately considers t-to-infinity and one-loop data. The authored theorem adds an explicit finite regulator, exact Q-invariant integration, and majorant hypotheses.

contents.name: S4 noncommutative regulator extension
contents.locator: Section 1, printed p.4 (PDF p.4), unnumbered paragraph between equations (1.5) and (1.6).
contents.support: The source explicitly assumes, without constructing it, the S4 extension of the noncommutative R4 regulator and its agreement near the poles. The theorem preserves this limit and does not claim that its separate finite-dimensional regulator exists.

sources.title: Vasilis Peelaers, 4d N=2 Localization lecture notes
sources.actual_read_extent: Retrieved the complete 21-page lecture note and read the full S4 conformal-Killing-spinor and localization-overview passage. The note states measure-invariance and Q-closure hypotheses, identifies the S4 Q-square, and warns that Q must close off shell; it explicitly defers the localization argument to a later lecture.
sources.limitations: This is an independent full lecture treatment of the S4 background, but it does not provide the deferred localization proof or construct the continuum measure. Its schematic localization formula is not used as a theorem.

contents.name: Four-dimensional rigid supersymmetry and Q-square background
contents.support: The lecture notes give an independent 4D background and supercharge-square treatment; the local definition reuses the exact established background interface and keeps the finite field-space realization separate.

contents.name: Localization measure and off-shell assumptions
contents.support: The notes state measure and off-shell conditions rather than construct a continuum measure or prove the continuum Ward identity. The theorem therefore states explicit finite-dimensional Q-invariance and majorant hypotheses.
